title: Perfect pseudo-coherent tensor tests on flat algebraic spaces
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the full subcategory with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. A perfect complex is etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Derived tensor and pullback use K-flat resolutions, and derived global sections use K-injective resolutions. Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a separated flat morphism of finite presentation. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion; flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts, and finite presentation includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Let $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. Suppose $R\Gamma(X,E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}K)$ [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology] is pseudo-coherent in $D(A)$ for every perfect $E$. Here pseudo-coherence over $A$ is [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Then $K$ is pseudo-coherent on $X$: etale locally on affine scheme charts it is represented by a bounded-above complex of finite free structure modules.

source.place: Tags 0GFJ (lemma-characterize-pseudo-coh-improved) and 0DII (lemma-relative-pseudo-coherent-is-moot), flat locally finitely presented case.

proof.text: The affine base $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply the finite-presentation qcqs-source lemma to $f$ to obtain that $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. This uses the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness included in finite presentation, not properness.

For every perfect $P$, choose the bounded-above finite-free model of $R\Gamma(X,P\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)$ supplied by pseudo-coherence. In degrees above its last nonzero term its cohomology is zero. The perfect tensor-test upper-bound criterion now gives an integer $b$ such that $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for $i>b$. The individual test bounds need not be uniform.

Apply the perfect-to-pseudo-coherent test lemma to $X$, $A$, and $K$. The qcqs hypothesis is step 1, the required upper bound is step 2, and the perfect-test hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis of the item. It follows that $R\Gamma(X,E\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)$ is pseudo-coherent in $D(A)$ for every pseudo-coherent $E$.

The pseudo-coherent tensor-test criterion applies to step 3 because $f$ is separated and of finite presentation and $K$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. It gives pseudo-coherence of $K$ relative to $\operatorname{Spec}A$.

Apply the relative/absolute comparison with base scheme $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $Y=S$. The morphism is flat by hypothesis and locally of finite presentation by its finite-presentation assumption. Its relative pseudo-coherence from step 4 therefore implies that $K$ is pseudo-coherent on $X$, which means precisely the etale-local bounded-above finite-free models in the conclusion.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0GFJ, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coh-improved, followed by Tag 0DII, lemma-relative-pseudo-coherent-is-moot

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q130-64648b7eb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Item statement unchanged. The five steps follow Stacks 0GFJ (spaces-more-morphisms lemma-characterize-pseudo-coh-improved) and then 0DII. I read each against the source. (1) Spec A is qcqs, and lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source (06G5) makes X qcqs. The target is affine, so the two qc conventions agree. (2) A pseudo-coherent RΓ over A vanishes above some degree, and the new node lem-sfb-space-perfect-tensor-tests-upper-bound (0GFH (7)(b)=>(1), generator from 09IY folded in, per-P bounds) gives K bounded above. (3) The new 0CWH node (lemma-perfect-enough) has exactly the hypotheses: qcqs, K in D^-_QCoh, perfect tests. (4) The new 0CTT node gives relative pseudo-coherence for separated fp f. Its 'every square' relative definition is equivalent to Stacks' 'one covering square' by the lemma before definition-relative-pseudo-coherence. (5) The new 0DII node with S=Y=Spec A, flat and lfp, gives absolute pseudo-coherence; its relative definition is the same text as step 4's. Each new node is a distinct Stacks lemma strictly smaller than the item: statement-only, self-contained, correct tags and labels. I tested them on X empty, Spec A, an unbounded-above K, and the flatness-free counterexample A/I. Duplicate search: tag grep over the DAG; every space pseudo-coherence node (def-sfb-space-relative-perfect, relative-perfect fibre and base change, 0GFI lower-bound detector, rhom-quasicoherent) and the scheme analogues; blueprint latest. No duplicate found. Batch-5 flags: def-trf-algebraic-space and def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module are general definitions. The closure of lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source reaches only foundational trf algebraic-space facts (fibre products, atlas tests, surjective composition), not steps of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so I accept them. The tool_use lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs is a generic Mathlib leaf; accepted. No SGA. Minor nit, not a fault: 'point space' is not linked to def-a1-space-point-topology, as in the sibling nodes.
